concepts: same signature twice is a compile-time error
questions.question: What is the type of error, if any, when two methods have the same method signature?
questions.solution: (c) Syntax error. Two methods with identical signatures in one class cannot be told apart, so the compiler reports an error (syntax/compile-time error).

questions.question:
The advantage/s of user-defined methods are/is:
(i) Reusability
(ii) Complexity
(iii) Modularity
questions.solution: (d) (i) and (iii). Methods let code be reused and divide a program into modules; they reduce, not add, complexity.

concepts: formal parameters appear in the method definition
questions.question: Parameters which receive the values from the called method are termed as _______ parameters.
questions.solution: (b) formal. The parameters declared in the method definition receive the values passed in the method call; they are formal parameters (the values passed are actual parameters).

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid method prototype?

options.c: public int perform (int a, int b)
options.d: public perform int (int a, int b)

questions.solution: (c) public int perform (int a, int b). A prototype needs access specifier, return type, name, then comma-separated parameters.

questions.topic: Invoking a method with matching arguments
concepts: argument order and type must match parameters
questions.question: Which of the following is the CORRECT statement to invoke the method with the prototype int display(int a, char ch)?
questions.solution: (d) int m = display(45,'A');. Arguments must match the parameter list in order: an int first, then a char.

concepts: String methods are called on a String object
questions.question: Which of the following is the CORRECT java statement to convert the word RESPECT to lowercase?
questions.solution: (b) "RESPECT".toLowerCase( );. toLowerCase() is an instance method (correct capitalisation) invoked on the String.

concepts: wrapper classes start with capital letters
questions.question:
Which of the following are Wrapper classes?
(i) Boolean
(ii) boolean
(iii) character
(iv) Character
questions.solution: (a) (i) and (iv). Boolean and Character are wrapper classes; boolean is a primitive type and "character" is not a Java type.

questions.question: Conversion of a wrapper class to its corresponding primitive type is known as :
questions.solution: (a) unboxing. Converting a wrapper object (e.g. Integer) to its primitive (int) is unboxing; the reverse is autoboxing.

questions.question: The String method, which results only in a positive integer, is :
questions.solution: (d) length. indexOf and lastIndexOf return -1 when not found and compareTo may be negative; length() never returns a negative value.

questions.question: The method to convert a String to double is:
questions.solution: (c) Double.parseDouble(String). Double.parseDouble takes the String to be converted as its argument.

questions.question: The java statement System.out.println(x[x.length]) results in:
questions.solution: (c) run time error. Index x.length is one past the last index, so ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown at run time (it compiles fine).

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid array declaration statement to store the Gender of 80 employees [ 'M'-male, 'F'-female, 'T'-transgender ]?
questions.solution: (b) char gender[] = new char[80];. Java arrays are declared with [] and the size is given with new.

questions.topic: Order of statements to input an array
concepts: declare array and Scanner before the loop
questions.solution: (b) (ii), (iii), (iv), (i). Create the array and the Scanner first, then the loop, whose body reads each element.

concepts: bubble sort compares and swaps adjacent elements
questions.question:
In the bubble sort technique, during each iteration of the inner loop, two adjacent elements are __________ and __________.
(i) compared
(ii) swapped
(iii) selected
(iv) deleted
questions.solution: (a) (i) and (ii). Adjacent elements are compared and swapped if they are out of order.

questions.question: What is the highest index of any array with 100 elements?
questions.solution: (c) 99. Indices run from 0 to length - 1 = 99.

concepts: dividing a task into methods = modularity
questions.question: Mr. Sanjay is an event manager, he plans and allots duties to each of his subordinates to handle different events. In a program, a task is divided into simple methods. Name the feature used in these contexts.
questions.solution: (b) Modularity. Splitting a big task into smaller independent units (methods) is modularity.

questions.question: Raj was asked to accept the phone number which has 10 digits, using the appropriate method of Scanner class. Which of the following statement he must choose?
questions.solution: (c) Ob.nextLong(). A 10-digit number can exceed the int range (2147483647), so it must be read as a long.

questions.question: Raj wanted to count the number of digits in a given number without using a loop. Which of the following statements is correct to perform the above?
questions.solution: (a) String.valueOf(n).length(). Converting the number to a String and taking its length counts the digits; an int has no length() method.

questions.question: Sham was asked to encode a string S, by replacing the letter E with #. Select the appropriate statement:
questions.solution: (c) S.replace('E', '#'). replace takes the old character first and the new character second.

questions.question:
Assertion: Property by virtue of which one class acquires the properties of another class is termed as Inheritance.
Reason: Inheritance promotes reusability.

options.a: Assertion is true, Reason is false.
options.b: Assertion is true, Reason is true.
options.c: Assertion is false, Reason is false.
options.d: Assertion is false, Reason is true.

questions.solution: (b) Assertion is true, Reason is true.. Both are true: the definition of inheritance is correct and inheriting existing code promotes reusability.

concepts: overloaded methods differ in number/type of arguments
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true for polymorphism?

options.a: All methods have the same name.
options.b: Methods are invoked based on the arguments.
options.c: Methods should have the same number and the same type of arguments.
options.d: It is a principle of OOPs.

questions.solution: (c) Methods should have the same number and the same type of arguments.. Overloaded methods must differ in the number or type of arguments; identical argument lists would be a compile error.

concepts: explicit cast of char to int
questions.question: Which of the following is a valid initialisation statement?
questions.solution: (c) int z = (int) 'x';. Casting the char 'x' to int gives 120; the others assign a String, a double and a boolean to int.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a valid statement to print the following sentence:
Raj said "Good morning"
questions.solution: (c) System.out.println("Raj said \"Good morning\" ");. The escape sequence \" places a double-quote character inside a String literal.

questions.question:
Which data structure is represented in the above picture?
[Picture: an ice-cube tray with 2 rows of 7 compartments each.]
(i) A two-dimensional array with 2 rows and seven columns.
(ii) A one-dimensional array with 14 elements.
questions.solution: (b) Only (i). The tray is laid out as a grid of 2 rows x 7 columns, i.e. a two-dimensional array.
questions.figure_desc: Photo of a blue ice-cube tray with 2 rows of 7 compartments.

concepts: condition tested before body = entry controlled
questions.question:
What is the type of looping statement depicted in the above picture?
[Flowchart: Start -> "While Condition" decision; True -> Command -> back to the condition; False -> End.]
questions.solution: (a) Entry controlled loop. The condition is checked before the command executes, so it is an entry-controlled (while) loop.
questions.figure_desc: Flowchart of a while loop: condition checked first, True leads to Command and back, False leads to End.

questions.question:
What is the process done in the above picture?
[Picture: the list B, D, A, C on the left, an arrow, and the list A, B, C, D on the right.]

options.a: Sorting the list in descending order
options.b: Searching the character in the list
options.c: Sorting the list in ascending order.

questions.solution: (c) Sorting the list in ascending order.. B D A C is rearranged into A B C D, i.e. sorted in ascending order.
questions.figure_desc: Coloured letter tiles B, D, A, C rearranged into A, B, C, D.

concepts: linear search checks elements one by one
questions.question:
Name the method of search depicted in the above picture.
[Picture: Search '6' - arrows hop element by element through 3, 8, 12 and stop at 6 in the array 3 8 12 6 10 2.]
questions.solution: (d) Linear Search. Each element is checked in sequence from the start until 6 is found - linear search (the array is not even sorted, so binary search is impossible).
questions.figure_desc: Array 3 8 12 6 10 2 with arrows hopping from the first element to 6 for Search '6'.

questions.question:
Name the feature of Java depicted in the above picture.
[Picture: a boy - "In Shopping malls behave like CUSTOMER", "In Bus behave like PASSENGER", "In School behave like STUDENT", "At Home behave like SON".]
questions.solution: (c) Polymorphism. The same person takes many forms depending on the context - polymorphism.
questions.figure_desc: Boy shown behaving as customer, passenger, student and son in different places.

questions.question:
Name the data types in order from top, given in the above picture.
[Picture, top to bottom: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."; 578; \n; 51.048053]
questions.solution: (b) String, int, char, double. A sentence in quotes is a String, 578 an int, \n a char (escape sequence) and 51.048053 a double.
questions.figure_desc: Four literals stacked: a quoted sentence, 578, \n and 51.048053.

concepts: array with decimal values is double
questions.question:
How many bytes are occupied by the above two-dimensional array?
The array (4 rows x 4 columns):
156  20     154  20
130  20     130  20
162  17.67  161  20
158  17.5   154  20
questions.solution: (b) 128 bytes. The array contains decimal values (17.67, 17.5), so it must be double; 4 x 4 = 16 elements x 8 bytes = 128 bytes.

questions.topic: Writing a Java expression with brackets
questions.question: A girl wanted to calculate the sum of two numbers stored as a and b multiplied by 7. Select the appropriate Java expression.
questions.solution: (c) (a+b)*7. The sum must be formed first, so a+b is bracketed before multiplying by 7.

questions.question: The sum of a[1] and a[3] in the array int a[]={20,40,60,80,100} is:
questions.solution: (c) 120. a[1] = 40 and a[3] = 80, so the sum is 120.

questions.question: State which access specifier is less restrictive.
questions.solution: (d) public. public members are accessible from everywhere, so it is the least restrictive.

questions.question: The AMB hotel gives the amount to be paid by the customer as an integer, which of the following Math method rounds off the bill in decimals to an integer?
questions.solution: (a) Math.round(). Math.round() rounds a decimal value to the nearest whole number (returns long/int).

concepts: overloaded constructors need different parameter lists
questions.question:
Assertion: A class can have multiple constructors
Reason: Multiple constructors are defined with same set of arguments.

options.a: Assertion is true, Reason is false.
options.b: Both assertion and Reason are false.
options.c: Both assertion and Reason are true.
options.d: Assertion is false, Reason is true.

questions.solution: (a) Assertion is true, Reason is false.. A class can have many (overloaded) constructors, but they must differ in their parameter lists, so the Reason is false.

concepts: array elements share one data type
questions.question:
Assertion: An array can store elements of different data types
Reason: An array is a user-defined data type with multiple values of the same data type but a different memory index.

options.a: Assertion is true, Reason is false.
options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are false.
options.c: Both Assertion and Reason are true.
options.d: Assertion is false, Reason is true.

questions.solution: (d) Assertion is false, Reason is true.. All elements of an array have the same data type, so the Assertion is false; the Reason correctly describes an array (a composite / user-defined type of same-type values at different indices).

questions.question: The output of the statement Math.ceil(89.9)+Math.floor(90.5) is:
questions.solution: (c) 180.0. Math.ceil(89.9) = 90.0 and Math.floor(90.5) = 90.0; both return double, so the sum is 180.0.

questions.question: The output of the statement "TIGER".indexOf('G') is:
questions.solution: (b) 2. T0 I1 G2, so indexOf returns 2.

concepts: ternary returns a value, not a statement
questions.solution: (b) System.out.println(a>b? "Honest": "Sincere");. The ternary operator yields a value, which println then prints; it cannot contain void statements or stand alone.

questions.question:
The two Java statement are used to check for the equality of the strings "COP" and "cop" are as follows:
"COP".equals("cop")
"COP".equalsIgnoreCase("cop")
The output of the above statements is:
questions.solution: (a) false, true. equals() is case-sensitive (false); equalsIgnoreCase() ignores case (true).

questions.topic: Memory of arrays of different types
questions.question:
Arrange the following in the descending order of number of bytes occupied.
(i) char x[20]
(ii) int a[4][2]
(iii) double b[6]
questions.solution: (b) (iii), (i), (ii). double b[6] = 6 x 8 = 48 bytes; char x[20] = 20 x 2 = 40 bytes; int a[4][2] = 8 x 4 = 32 bytes.

concepts: bubble sort compares adjacent pairs left to right
questions.solution: (a) {1,2,5,3}. The next comparison is of the adjacent pair 5 and 2; since 5 > 2 they are swapped, giving {1,2,5,3}.
